reverse_expectations.model: 10-year constant owner-cash-per-share growth followed by terminal owner-cash multiple
reverse_expectations.interpretation: The current price embeds mid-single-digit long-run owner-cash/share growth, which is achievable if Salesforce retains workflow/data control and Agentforce/Data 360 monetize successfully, but it is not a no-growth valuation. The post-Q2 price rebound has reduced the expectation gap.

permanent_loss_stress.assumptions: Owner cash/share -6% CAGR years 1-5 then flat; 12% discount; 9x terminal. AI-native agents bypass Salesforce interfaces, seat economics contract, acquisitions underperform and leverage limits capital allocation.

bear.assumptions: Owner cash/share flat years 1-5 then +2% years 6-10; 11% discount; 13x terminal. Core organic growth stays mid-single digit, Agentforce monetization disappoints and leverage/interest constrain per-share compounding.

base.assumptions: Owner cash/share +7% CAGR years 1-5 and +5% years 6-10; 10% discount; 18x terminal. CRM system-of-record and data/metadata moat persist, Agentforce/Data 360 become meaningful growth layers, but organic growth remains below reported acquisition-assisted growth.

bull.assumptions: Owner cash/share +11% CAGR years 1-5 and +8% years 6-10; 9% discount; 21x terminal. Agentforce becomes the enterprise action/orchestration layer, Data 360/Informatica deepen data gravity, Slack becomes a major agent interface and margin/productivity gains persist.

warnings: Scenario fair values are decision ranges, not price targets.
FCFE-style owner cash already reflects interest expense; debt is therefore not subtracted again in the per-share scenario model.
The March 2026 debt-funded ASR materially reduces share count but also raises financial risk and future interest burden; EPS growth from the ASR is not equivalent to operating growth.
Agentforce ARR definition broadened in Q2 FY27, reducing strict comparability of the reported growth rate.
